t.1.163.1: Vasiṣṭha said: This daughter of yours named Tapatī, the younger sister of Sāvitrī, I ask of you on behalf of Saṃvaraṇa, O Vibhāvasu.
t.1.163.3: Thus addressed by him, Savitṛ, resolved in his mind, "I shall give her," greeted the brahmin warmly, and the Maker of Day replied to him.
t.1.163.2: For that king Saṃvaraṇa, of great renown, a knower of dharma and artha and noble of mind, is a fitting husband for your daughter, O sky-farer.
t.1.163.7: That king, possessed by love, his inmost self wholly fixed on her, beheld the divine maiden Tapatī of the lovely smile approaching together with Vasiṣṭha, and, overjoyed, he shone forth all the more brightly.
t.1.163.6: Then Vasiṣṭha, having been dismissed, came back once more to the place where that bull of the Kurus, of widely renowned fame, was.
t.1.163.8: When that king's twelve-night penance had been completed, the blessed seer Vasiṣṭha, whose soul was pure, arrived.
t.1.163.10: Then, on that best of mountains, frequented by gods and Gandharvas, that bull among men took the hand of Tapatī according to the rite.
t.1.163.9: Having propitiated with austerity the boon-granting god, the lord of rays, the sovereign, Saṃvaraṇa obtained his wife through the power of Vasiṣṭha alone.
t.1.163.11: Permitted by Vasiṣṭha, the royal sage desired to sport with his wife on that very mountain.
t.1.163.12: Then the king appointed that very minister over the city and the realm, over the mounts and the armies.
t.1.163.13: Then Vasiṣṭha, having taken leave of the king, departed; and the king too, like an immortal, sported on that mountain.
t.1.163.14: Then for twelve years the king took his delight on that mountain, in its forests and in its waters, together with that very wife of his.
t.1.163.15: For twelve years the thousand-eyed one sent no rain at all upon that king's city, nor anywhere at all in his kingdom.
t.1.163.16: Then, with its men tormented by hunger, joyless and become like corpses, that city was like the city of the king of the departed, thronged with ghosts.
t.1.163.17: Then, seeing that state of affairs, that same blessed seer, the righteous-souled Vasiṣṭha, approached the best of kings.
t.1.163.18: And he brought that tiger among kings, together with Tapatī, to that city, O king, after he had dwelt away for twelve years.
t.1.163.19: Then, when that tiger among kings had entered his city once more, the slayer of the enemies of the gods rained there as before.
t.1.163.20: Then that city, together with its kingdom, rejoiced with supreme joy, cherished as it was by that foremost of kings whose soul was purified.
t.1.163.21: Then for twelve years the lord of men again offered sacrifices, together with his wife Tapatī, just as Śakra, the lord of the Maruts, does.
t.1.163.23: On her, on Tapatī, King Saṃvaraṇa begot Kuru; therefore, O Arjuna, best of those who practise austerities, you are a Tāpatya.
t.1.163.22: Such was the illustrious Tapatī, your ancestress, the daughter of Vivasvat, O Pārtha, through whom you are deemed a Tāpatya.
t.1.163.4: Saṃvaraṇa is the best of kings, and you, O sage, are the best of seers; Tapatī is the most excellent of women. What else is there but to give her away?
t.1.163.5: Then Tapana himself gave Tapatī, flawless in every limb, to the great-souled Vasiṣṭha on behalf of Saṃvaraṇa. The great seer then received that maiden Tapatī.
